mishnayos.summary: The Torah has thirty-six sins that are so serious that one who does them on purpose gets kares. This mishnah lists all of them.

chunks.en: There are thirty-six sins in the Torah that bring kares.
chunks.explain: Kares is a very serious punishment from Hashem.

words.note: Sins whose punishment is kares, being cut off.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother,
or with his father's wife,
or with his daughter-in-law.

words.note: His son's wife.

chunks.en: One who sins with another man,
or sins with an animal,
and a woman who sins with an animal.
One who sins with a woman and her daughter,
or with a married woman.
One who sins with his sister,
or with his father's sister,
or with his mother's sister,
or with his wife's sister,
or with his brother's wife,
or with the wife of his father's brother,
or with a niddah.
One who curses Hashem's Name, and one who serves idols,
and one who gives some of his children to the Molech idol,

words.note: An idol that people served by passing children through fire.

chunks.en: and a ba'al ov,

words.note: A ba'al ov claims to talk with the dead.

chunks.en: one who breaks Shabbos,
and one who is tamei and ate holy food,
and one who goes into the Beis HaMikdash while tamei,
one who eats chelev,

words.note: Certain fat of an animal that the Torah forbids to eat.

chunks.en: or blood, or nosar,

words.note: Meat of a korban left over after the time to eat it.

chunks.en: or piggul, and one who shechts and offers a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash,

words.note: A korban made unfit by planning to eat it after its time.

chunks.en: one who eats chametz on Pesach,
and one who eats or does work on Yom Kippur,
one who mixes the special oil,
and one who mixes the ketores,

words.note: The special incense burned in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and one who rubs himself with the shemen hamishchah.

words.note: The special oil Moshe made to anoint the Kohanim and the Mishkan.

chunks.en: Also Korban Pesach and bris milah, which are mitzvos to do.

mishnayos.summary: For these sins, one who does them on purpose gets kares, and one who does them by mistake brings a chatas. Rabbi Meir and the Sages say which sins are different.

chunks.he: עַל אֵלּוּ חַיָּבִים עַל זְדוֹנָם כָּרֵת,
chunks.en: For these sins, one who does them on purpose gets kares,
chunks.st: For any of these prohibitions, one is liable to receive karet for its intentional violation

chunks.en: and one who does them by mistake brings a chatas,
chunks.st: and to bring a sin offering for its unwitting violation.

chunks.he: וְעַל לֹא הוֹדַע שֶׁלָּהֶן אָשָׁם תָּלוּי,
chunks.en: and one who is not sure if he sinned brings an asham taluy,
chunks.st: And for their violation in a case where it is unknown to him whether or not he transgressed, he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: which provides provisional atonement until he discovers whether or not he transgressed.

words.note: Hanging: brought when one is not sure he sinned.

chunks.en: except for one who makes the Beis HaMikdash or its holy things tamei,
chunks.st: This is the halakha for all of the transgressions listed above except for one who defiles the Temple, i.e., he enters the Temple while ritually impure, or partakes of its consecrated items
chunks.stMore: while ritually impure.

chunks.en: because he brings a korban oleh v'yored.
chunks.st: In these cases he does not bring a provisional guilt offering because he is obligated to bring a sliding-scale offering for a definite transgression.

words.note: A korban that goes up and down: a rich person brings more, a poor person less.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: also one who curses Hashem does not bring them,
chunks.st: The halakha is the same even with regard to the one who blasphemes,

chunks.en: as it says (Bamidbar 15),
chunks.st: as it is stated
chunks.stMore: with regard to the sin offering:

chunks.he: תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה,
chunks.en: "You shall have one law for one who does it by mistake."
chunks.st: “You shall have one law for him who performs the action unwittingly” (Numbers 15:29),

chunks.en: This leaves out one who curses Hashem,
chunks.st: excluding one who blasphemes,

chunks.en: because he does not do an action.
chunks.st: as he does not perform an action but sins with speech.

mishnayos.summary: When a woman loses a pregnancy, sometimes she brings a korban that is eaten, sometimes a korban that is not eaten, and sometimes no korban at all. This mishnah lists the first group.

chunks.en: Some women bring a korban and it is eaten,
and some bring one but it is not eaten,
and some do not bring one at all.
These bring a korban and it is eaten:
A woman who lost a pregnancy that looked like an animal, a wild animal, or a bird.

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
But the Sages say,
it must have the shape of a person.
A woman who lost a pregnancy shaped like a sandal,

words.note: A flat shape, like a flat fish.

chunks.en: or the afterbirth,
or a sac with a shape inside,
or one that did not come out whole,
and also a maidservant who lost a pregnancy,
brings a korban and it is eaten.

mishnayos.summary: Sometimes a woman brings a korban but it is not eaten, because we are not sure she really needed it. Rabbi Yosei says when two women may bring one korban together.

chunks.en: These bring a korban, but it is not eaten:
chunks.st: And these women bring sin offerings but their sin offerings are not eaten:

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy and does not know what it was,
chunks.st: One who miscarries and does not know the nature of what she miscarried;

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: and also two women who lost pregnancies,
chunks.st: and two women who miscarried,

chunks.he: אַחַת מִמִּין פְּטוּר וְאַחַת מִמִּין חוֹבָה.
chunks.en: one of a kind that needs no korban, and one of a kind that needs a korban.
chunks.st: in a case where one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is exempt from bringing an offering and the other one miscarried a fetus of a type for which a woman is liable to bring an offering, and they do not know which miscarried which type.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָלְכוּ זוֹ לְמִזְרָח וְזוֹ לְמַעֲרָב.
chunks.en: When is this? When one went to the east and the other to the west.
chunks.st: When is their sin offering not eaten? It is when both women went to different places within the Temple to bring their offerings, e.g., this woman went to the east and that woman went to the west.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן עוֹמְדוֹת כְּאַחַת,
chunks.en: But if both of them were standing together,
chunks.st: But if both of them were standing together,

chunks.en: they bring a korban, and it is eaten.
chunks.st: both of them together bring one sin offering, and it is eaten.

mishnayos.summary: Some women who lose a pregnancy do not bring a korban at all, because what came out was not a baby. Rabbi Shimon argues about one case.

chunks.en: These do not bring a korban:
A woman who lost a sac full of water,
full of blood,
or full of colored things,

chunks.he: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים,
chunks.en: a woman who lost something like fish, grasshoppers, or creeping creatures,
a woman who lost a pregnancy on the fortieth day,
and a baby born through the side.
Rabbi Shimon says she must bring a korban for a baby born through the side.

mishnayos.summary: After a girl is born, the mother brings her korban on the eighty-first day. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about a woman who loses a pregnancy on the night before that day: does she need another korban?

chunks.en: A woman who lost a pregnancy on the night before the eighty-first day,

words.en: a woman who lost a pregnancy

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say she does not need another korban,
and Beis Hillel say she does.
Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
"What is the difference between the night of the eighty-first
and the eighty-first day?
If they are the same for tumah,
shouldn't they be the same for the korban?"
Beis Shammai said to them,

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: "No! If you said this about a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day,
that is because she came into a time that is
fit to bring a korban.
Will you say the same about one who lost on the night before the eighty-first,
who did not come into a time that is
fit to bring a korban?"
Beis Hillel said to them,
"But look at a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day
that falls on Shabbos. It proves our point:
she did not come into a time that is fit
to bring a korban, and still she must bring a korban!"
Beis Shammai said to them,

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים
chunks.en: "No! If you said this about a woman who lost a pregnancy on the eighty-first day
that falls on Shabbos,
that is because, even though Shabbos is not
fit for the korban of one person,
it is fit for a korban of the whole community.
Will you say the same about one who lost on the night before the eighty-first,
when the night is not fit, not for a korban
of one person and not for a korban of the community?
And the tumah of the blood does not prove anything,
because a woman who lost a pregnancy before her eighty days were complete
is tamei,
and still she does not need to bring a korban."

mishnayos.summary: A woman who needs many korbanos of birds may bring just one and then eat from korbanos. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught this to bring down the price of birds.

chunks.en: A woman who is not sure about five
times of being a zavah and not sure about five births,

words.note: Times of being a zavah, a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: brings one korban,
and then she may eat from korbanos,
and she does not have to bring the rest.
If she had five births for sure,
or five times of being a zavah for sure,
she brings one korban,
and then she may eat from korbanos,
but she still has to bring the rest.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָמְדוּ קִנִּים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם בְּדִינְרֵי זָהָב.
chunks.en: Once, a pair of birds cost a gold dinar in Yerushalayim.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
"I swear by this house of Hashem,

words.note: The Beis HaMikdash, where the Shechinah rests.

chunks.en: I will not go to sleep tonight
until they cost silver dinars!"
He went into the Beis Din and taught:

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חָמֵשׁ לֵדוֹת וַדָּאוֹת,
chunks.en: A woman who has five births for sure,
or five times of being a zavah for sure,
brings one korban,
and then she may eat from korbanos,
and she does not have to bring the rest.
That same day, the price of a pair of birds went down to a quarter of a silver dinar.

mishnayos.summary: Four kinds of people still need to bring a korban before they may eat holy food. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov adds a ger and a nazir.

chunks.en: There are four who are "missing atonement," and four
who bring a korban for sinning on purpose just as for sinning by mistake.
These are the ones missing atonement:
a zav, a zavah,

words.note: A man with a kind of tumah that comes from his body.
A woman with a kind of tumah that comes from her body.

chunks.en: a woman who had a baby, and a metzora.

words.en: and the woman who had a baby

words.note: A person with tzaraas, a skin sickness sent as a punishment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,

chunks.he: גֵּר, מְחֻסַּר כַּפָּרָה עַד שֶׁיִּזָּרֵק עָלָיו הַדָּם.
chunks.en: a ger is missing atonement until the blood of his korban is sprinkled for him,

words.note: A person who became Jewish.

chunks.en: and a nazir, for his wine, his haircut, and his tumah.

mishnayos.summary: Here are four people who bring the same korban whether they sinned on purpose or by mistake.

chunks.en: These bring a korban for sinning on purpose just as for sinning by mistake:
One who sins with the shifchah,

words.note: A maidservant who is promised to be married to a Jewish slave.

chunks.en: and a nazir who became tamei,
and one who falsely swears he knows no testimony,
and one who falsely swears about something left with him.

words.note: Something that someone gave him to watch.

mishnayos.summary: Some people bring only one korban even though they sinned many times. Others bring a korban oleh v'yored. This mishnah begins listing the first group.

chunks.en: Five people bring one korban
for many sins,
and five bring a korban oleh v'yored.

words.note: A korban that goes up and down: a rich person brings more, a poor person less.

chunks.en: These bring one korban
for many sins:
One who sins with the shifchah many times,
and a nazir who became tamei many times,

chunks.he: וְהַמְקַנֵּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: and one who warns his wife about many men,
chunks.explain: He warned her not to be alone with them.

chunks.en: and a metzora who got tzaraas many times.
If he brought his birds and then got tzaraas again,
they do not count for him
until he brings his chatas.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
until he brings his asham.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah finishes the list of people who bring one korban for many times, and lists who brings a korban oleh v'yored. Then it explains how the shifchah is different from other forbidden relationships.

chunks.en: A woman who had many babies,
or lost a girl pregnancy within eighty days, and again
lost a girl pregnancy within eighty days,
or a woman who lost twins.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
she brings a korban for the first and does not
bring for the second.
She brings for the third and does not
bring for the fourth.
These bring a korban oleh v'yored:
for hearing the voice of an oath,
chunks.explain: He swore falsely that he knew no testimony.

chunks.en: and for saying an oath with the lips,
chunks.explain: He swore falsely about something else.

chunks.en: and for making the Beis HaMikdash or its holy foods tamei,
and a woman who had a baby, and a metzora.

words.en: and the woman who had a baby

chunks.he: וּמַה בֵּין הַשִּׁפְחָה לְבֵין כָּל הָעֲרָיוֹת.
chunks.en: What is the difference between the shifchah and all the other forbidden relationships?
She is not the same as them, not
in the punishment and not in the korban.
For all the forbidden relationships one brings a chatas, but for the shifchah an asham.
For all the forbidden relationships one brings a female animal,
and for the shifchah a male.
In all the forbidden relationships,
both the man and the woman
are the same for lashes and for a korban.

chunks.he: וּבַשִּׁפְחָה לֹא הִשְׁוָה אֶת הָאִישׁ לָאִשָּׁה
chunks.en: But with the shifchah, the Torah did not make the man the same as the woman

chunks.he: בַּמַּכּוֹת וְלֹא אֶת הָאִשָּׁה לָאִישׁ בַּקָּרְבָּן.
chunks.en: for lashes, and not the woman the same as the man for a korban.
In all the forbidden relationships,
the Torah counts just starting the sin like finishing it,
and he must bring a korban for each and every time.
This is a stricter rule for the shifchah:
the Torah made one who did it on purpose like one who did it by mistake.
chunks.explain: Both of them bring an asham.

words.en: one who does it on purpose
like one who does it by mistake

mishnayos.summary: Who is the shifchah that the Torah talks about? Rabbi Akiva says she is half a maidservant and half free; Rabbi Yishmael says she is a full maidservant.

chunks.en: Who is the shifchah?
chunks.st: Who is the espoused maidservant in question?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁחֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: Any woman who is half a maidservant and half free,
chunks.st: It is any woman who is half-maidservant half-free woman,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a maidservant who belonged to two masters, one of whom liberated her,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 19),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "and she was redeemed but not redeemed."
chunks.explain: She was set free only partly.
chunks.st: “And she was redeemed and not redeemed” (Leviticus 19:20),
chunks.stMore: which means that she was partially but not completely redeemed.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: she is a full maidservant.
chunks.st: An espoused maidservant is a full-fledged maidservant whose status is certain,
chunks.stMore: as the language of the verse does not mean redeemed and not redeemed; it is simply a way of stating that she was not redeemed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: All the forbidden relationships are written out in the Torah,
chunks.st: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated in the Torah,

chunks.en: so what is left?
chunks.st: and we have

chunks.en: We only have one who is half
chunks.st: no exception other than one who is half-maidservant

chunks.en: a maidservant and half free.
chunks.st: half-free woman.

mishnayos.summary: In other forbidden relationships, a child, a sleeping person, or one who sinned by mistake is treated differently from the other one.

chunks.en: In all the forbidden relationships,
if one is grown up and one is a child,
the child is free from punishment.
If one is awake and one is asleep,
the sleeping one is free.
If one did it by mistake and one on purpose,
the one who did it by mistake brings a chatas, and the one who did it on purpose gets kares.

mishnayos.summary: What if witnesses say a person ate chelev by mistake? It depends on how many witnesses there are and whether he agrees. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about one case.

chunks.en: If people told him, "You ate chelev,"
chunks.st: If witnesses said to a person: We saw that you ate forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings a chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering if he did so unwittingly.

chunks.en: If one witness says he ate, and another witness
chunks.st: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and a witness

chunks.en: says he did not eat,
chunks.st: says: He did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: or one woman says he ate, and another woman
chunks.st: or if a woman says: He ate forbidden fat, and a woman

chunks.en: says he did not eat,
chunks.st: says: He did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings an asham taluy.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: brought by one who is uncertain as to whether he committed a sin that requires a sin offering.

words.note: Brought when one is not sure he sinned.

chunks.en: If one witness says he ate, and he himself
chunks.st: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself

chunks.en: says, "I did not eat,"
chunks.st: says: I did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he is free. If two witnesses say he ate, and he himself
chunks.st: he is exempt. If two witnesses say: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself

chunks.en: says, "I did not eat,"
chunks.st: says: I did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he must bring a korban.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems him liable to bring a sin offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:
chunks.stMore: This conclusion can be derived a fortiori:

chunks.en: "If two witnesses can bring him to the harsh punishment of death,
chunks.st: If two witnesses could have brought him liability to receive the severe punishment of death,

chunks.en: can't they bring him to a korban, which is lighter?"
chunks.st: can they not bring him liability to sacrifice an offering, which is relatively lenient?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:
chunks.stMore: Witnesses are unable to render another person liable to bring an offering contrary to his statement,

chunks.he: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה לוֹמַר מֵזִיד הָיִיתִי:
chunks.en: "What if he wants to say, 'I did it on purpose'?"
chunks.explain: Then he would not bring a korban at all.
chunks.st: as what if he wishes to say: I did so intentionally, in which case he would be exempt from bringing an offering?

mishnayos.summary: When does one who eats forbidden foods bring one chatas, and when does he bring many? It depends on whether he ate one kind or many kinds.

chunks.en: If he ate chelev and more chelev in one time of forgetting,
chunks.explain: He did not find out in between that it was forbidden.
chunks.st: If one unwittingly ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat and then ate another olive-bulk of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in a case where he did not discover in the interim that fat is forbidden, or that the food he is eating is forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings only one chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

chunks.en: If he ate chelev, blood, nosar,
chunks.st: If one ate forbidden fat, and blood,

chunks.en: and piggul in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: and piggul, and notar in one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas for each one.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one of them.

chunks.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בְּמִינִין הַרְבֵּה מִמִּין אֶחָד.
chunks.en: This is a stricter rule for many kinds than for one kind.
chunks.st: This is a stringency that applies to one who eats several types of forbidden food and does not apply to one who eats one type of forbidden food.

chunks.en: And there is a stricter rule for one kind than for many kinds:
chunks.st: And a stringency that applies to one who eats one type of forbidden food and not to one who eats several types of forbidden food is

chunks.en: if he ate half a kezayis and then
chunks.st: that if one ate half an olive-bulk and then

chunks.en: ate another half a kezayis of the same kind,
chunks.st: ate another half an olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness, in a case where they were both from one type of forbidden food,

chunks.en: he is liable. If from two kinds, he is free.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering. If they were from two types, he is exempt,
chunks.stMore: because he did not eat an olive-bulk of any specific forbidden food.

mishnayos.summary: How slowly can a person eat a forbidden food and still be punished? Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue. The same time counts for tamei foods and for drinking wine before going into the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: How long may one take while eating them?
chunks.st: How much time can one expend while eating an olive-bulk of forbidden food and still be liable for violating the prohibition?

chunks.en: As long as it takes to eat roasted grain,
chunks.st: The duration is calculated as though he were eating toasted grain,
chunks.stMore: which one eats one kernel at a time. If he eats the olive-bulk of forbidden food within the amount of time it would take to eat an olive-bulk of toasted grain, he is liable.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: as long as the time from start
chunks.st: Unless the amount of time he expends from beginning to

chunks.en: to end is the time it takes to eat a peras.
chunks.st: end is more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf [peras] of bread, he is liable.

words.note: Half of a loaf of bread.

chunks.en: If one ate tamei foods,
chunks.st: Likewise, one who ate a quarter-loaf of ritually impure foods

chunks.en: or drank tamei drinks,
chunks.st: or drank a quarter-log of ritually impure liquids
chunks.stMore: within the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread is rendered unfit to partake of teruma, the portion of the produce designated for priests, until he becomes pure.

chunks.en: or drank a revi'is of wine and went into the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one drank a quarter-log of wine and entered the Temple,

words.note: A small amount, about one cup.

chunks.en: and stayed there as long as it takes to eat a peras, he is liable.
chunks.st: and he remained there for the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: if he stopped in the middle, or if he put
chunks.st: If he interrupted his drinking of the quarter-log of wine or if he placed

chunks.en: even a little water into it, he is free.
chunks.st: any amount of water into the wine, he is exempt.

mishnayos.summary: One bite of food can make a person bring four chataos and one asham. Rabbi Meir says that on Shabbos it could be even more.

chunks.en: A person can eat one time and must bring
chunks.st: There is a case where one can perform a single act of eating an olive-bulk of food and be liable

chunks.en: four chataos and one asham for it.
chunks.st: to bring four sin offerings and one guilt offering for it.

chunks.en: One who was tamei and ate chelev,
chunks.st: How so? This halakha applies to one who is ritually impure who ate forbidden fat,

chunks.en: and it was nosar,
chunks.st: and it was left over

chunks.en: from korbanos,
chunks.st: from a consecrated offering after the time allotted for its consumption [notar],

chunks.en: and it was Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: on Yom Kippur.
chunks.stMore: He is liable to bring sin offerings for eating forbidden fat and notar, for eating the meat of an offering while impure, and for eating on Yom Kippur. He is also liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: if it was Shabbos and he carried it out in his mouth,
chunks.st: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out from a private domain to a public domain while eating it,

chunks.en: he is liable for one more. They said to him,
chunks.st: he would be liable to bring an additional sin offering for performing prohibited labor on Shabbat. The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: "That is not the same kind of sin."
chunks.st: That liability is not from the same type of prohibition, as it is not due to the act of eating, and therefore, it should not be counted.

mishnayos.summary: One forbidden act can make a person bring six chataos, if the woman is forbidden to him in many ways at once.

chunks.en: A person can do one forbidden act
and must bring six chataos for it.
One who sins with his daughter
must bring for her because she is his daughter, his sister,
his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife,
a married woman, and a niddah.
And one who sins with his daughter's daughter

chunks.he: חַיָּב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בַּת בִּתּוֹ וְכַלָּתוֹ
chunks.en: must bring for her because she is his daughter's daughter, his daughter-in-law,

chunks.he: וַאֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו וְאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי
chunks.en: his wife's sister, his brother's wife, the wife of his father's
brother, a married woman, and a niddah.
Rabbi Yosei says,
if the grandfather broke the law and married her,
he must also bring for her because she is his father's wife.
And the same for one who sins with his wife's daughter,
or with his wife's daughter's daughter.

mishnayos.summary: One who sins with his mother-in-law can be forbidden to her in many ways at once. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Sages argue whether some of them count as separate sins.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother-in-law
must bring for her because she is his mother-in-law, his daughter-in-law,
his wife's sister, his brother's wife, the wife
of his father's brother, a married woman, and a niddah.
And the same for one who sins with his mother-in-law's mother,
or with his father-in-law's mother.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says,
one who sins with his mother-in-law
must bring for her because she is his mother-in-law,
his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother.
They said to him,
"All three of them are one kind of sin."

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua: if a person did several different forbidden things in one time of forgetting, does he bring one chatas or one for each? They answered from a similar case they had heard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
"I asked Rabban Gamliel and
Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market of Emmaus,

words.note: A town in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: where they went to buy an animal for the wedding feast
of Rabban Gamliel's son:

chunks.he: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו
chunks.en: One who sins with his sister, and with his father's sister,

chunks.he: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד מַהוּ,
chunks.en: and with his mother's sister, in one time of forgetting, what is the rule?
Must he bring one chatas for all of them,

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?
And they said to me,
'We did not hear about this.
But we did hear
that one who was with his five wives
when they were niddah, in one time of forgetting,

chunks.he: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
chunks.en: must bring a chatas for each and every one.'
And it seems to me that these things are a kal vachomer."

words.note: Kal vachomer: if a rule is true in an easier case, it is surely true in a harder one.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva asked whether a limb of an animal that is hanging loose makes things tamei. The Rabbis answered from what sick people in Yerushalayim used to do before Pesach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva asked them another question:
A limb of an animal that is hanging loose,
what is the rule? They said to him,
"We did not hear about this.
But we did hear about a limb of a person that is hanging loose,
that it is tahor.

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּךְ הָיוּ מֻכֵּי שְׁחִין שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם עוֹשִׂין,
chunks.en: This is what people sick with boils in Yerushalayim used to do:

chunks.he: הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ עֶרֶב פֶּסַח אֵצֶל הָרוֹפֵא
chunks.en: one would go to the doctor on Erev Pesach,

chunks.he: וְחוֹתְכוֹ עַד שֶׁהוּא מַנִּיחַ בּוֹ כִשְׂעֹרָה,
chunks.en: and the doctor cuts it almost all the way, leaving only a hair's width,
and sticks it onto a thorn,
and the sick man pulls away from it.
Then that man brings his Korban Pesach,
and the doctor brings his Korban Pesach.
And it seems to us that these things are a kal vachomer."

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva asked about one who did the same sin with five korbanos in one time of forgetting. Rabbi Yehoshua answered from the rule of me'ilah, but Rabbi Akiva showed why that proof does not work.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva asked them another question:
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט חֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בַּחוּץ בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: One who shechts five korbanos outside the Beis HaMikdash in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: With regard to one who unwittingly slaughters five offerings outside the Temple during one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: what is the rule? Must he bring one chatas for all of them,
chunks.st: what is the halakha? Is he liable to bring five sin offerings, one for each and every act of slaughter,

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?
chunks.st: or is he liable to bring one sin offering for all the acts of slaughter?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: "We did not hear about this."
chunks.st: We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: "I heard about one who eats from one korban
chunks.st: I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering

chunks.en: from five pots in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: from five different pots in which they were prepared, during one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: that he must bring a korban for each
chunks.st: that he is liable to bring five guilt offerings, which are for the meat prepared in each

chunks.en: and every one, because of me'ilah.
chunks.st: and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

words.note: Using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for oneself.

chunks.en: And I see that these things are a kal vachomer."
chunks.st: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference:
chunks.stMore: If one is liable to bring five guilt offerings for one offering prepared in five pots, all the more so is he liable to bring five sin offerings for slaughtering five offerings outside the Temple.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: "That is not what Rabbi Akiva asked them.
chunks.st: It was not that question that Rabbi Akiva asked them.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא, בְּאוֹכֵל נוֹתָר מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד,
chunks.en: Rather, about one who eats nosar from five korbanos in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: Rather, it was with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings during one lapse of awareness.

chunks.en: what is the rule? Must he bring one chatas for all of them,
chunks.st: What is the halakha? Is he liable to bring one sin offering for all the offerings from which he ate notar,

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?
chunks.st: or is he liable to bring five sin offerings, one for each and every one of the offerings from which he ate notar?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: 'We did not hear about this.'
chunks.st: We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: 'I heard about one who eats from one korban
chunks.st: I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering

chunks.en: from five pots in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: that was prepared in five different pots, during one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: that he must bring a korban for each
chunks.st: that he is liable to bring separate guilt offerings for the meat prepared in each

chunks.en: and every one, because of me'ilah.
chunks.st: and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: And I see that these things are a kal vachomer.'
chunks.st: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference:
chunks.stMore: If one is liable to bring five guilt offerings for one offering prepared in five pots, all the more so is he liable to bring five sin offerings for eating the notar of five separate offerings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: 'If it is a halachah you received,
chunks.st: If you are reporting a halakha that you received from your teachers
chunks.stMore: with regard to one who eats notar from five offerings,

chunks.en: we will accept it. But if it is from reasoning,
chunks.st: we will accept it, but if it is based merely on the a fortiori inference
chunks.stMore: from misuse of consecrated property,

chunks.en: there is an answer against it.'
chunks.st: there is a response that refutes the inference.

chunks.en: He said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: 'Answer!' He said to him,
chunks.st: Respond. Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִמְעִילָה שֶׁעָשָׂה בָהּ אֶת
chunks.en: 'No! If you said this about me'ilah, where the Torah made
chunks.st: And no; one cannot derive the halakha of notar through an a fortiori inference from misuse of consecrated property: If you said with regard to misuse
chunks.stMore: of consecrated property that one is liable to bring five guilt offerings, perhaps that is because there are additional stringent elements unique to misuse.

chunks.en: one who feeds others like one who eats, and one who lets others benefit like one who benefits,
chunks.st: As, with regard to misuse, the Torah established that the status of one who feeds another person sacrificial meat is like that of one who eats sacrificial meat, and the status of one who gives benefit to another from consecrated property that is not food is like that of one who derives benefit himself,
chunks.stMore: in that each is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse.

chunks.en: and joined me'ilah over a long time,
chunks.st: In addition, the Torah joined the misuse of consecrated property that was performed over an extended period,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if one derived benefit worth half a peruta one day and half a peruta the next, he is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse.

chunks.en: will you say the same about nosar,
chunks.st: Would you say the same with regard to notar,

chunks.en: which has none of these?'"
chunks.st: which has none of these halakhot?

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Akiva asked Rabbi Eliezer about one who does many melachos of the same kind on many Shabbosos in one time of forgetting. Rabbi Eliezer tried to prove that he brings many chataos, and Rabbi Akiva answered each proof.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
"I asked Rabbi Eliezer:
One who does many melachos on many Shabbosos,
all of the same kind of melachah,
in one time of forgetting,
what is the rule?
Must he bring one chatas for all of them,

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?'
He said to me,
'He must bring one for each and every one,
from a kal vachomer:
If for a niddah,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: where there are not many kinds of sins and many chataos,
one must bring a chatas for each time,

chunks.he: שַׁבָּת, שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: then Shabbos, where there are many kinds of sins and many chataos,
isn't it right that he must bring
one for each and every one?'
I said to him,
'No! If you said this about a niddah,
where there are two warnings,
since he is warned about the niddah
and the niddah is warned about him,
will you say the same about Shabbos,
where there is only one warning?'
He said to me,
'The case of young girls who are niddah will prove it,
where there is only one warning,
and still he must bring one for each and every time.'
I said to him,

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת,
chunks.en: 'No! If you said this about the young girls,

chunks.he: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן עַכְשָׁיו,
chunks.en: that even though there is no warning for them now,
there will be later,
will you say the same about Shabbos,
where there is not, not now
and not later?'
He said to me,
'One who sins with an animal will prove it.'
I said to him,
'An animal is like Shabbos.'"

mishnayos.summary: When a person is not sure whether he did a sin that needs a chatas, he brings an asham taluy. This mishnah gives examples.

chunks.en: If he is not sure whether he ate chelev
or did not eat it,
or even if he ate it,
but is not sure if it was the full amount
or not;
if chelev and permitted fat were in front of him,
and he ate one of them and does not
know which one he ate;
if his wife and his sister were with him in the house,
and he sinned by mistake with one of them and does not
know with which one he sinned;
if he mixed up Shabbos and a weekday,
and he did work on one of them and does not
know on which one he did it,
he brings an asham taluy.

mishnayos.summary: Just like a person can bring one chatas for many sins, he can bring one asham taluy for many doubts. Then Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about one who surely sinned but does not know which sin it was.

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִם אָכַל חֵלֶב וְחֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם
chunks.en: Just as if he ate chelev and more chelev in one time

chunks.he: אֶחָד אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא חַטָּאת אַחַת,
chunks.en: of forgetting, he brings only one chatas,
so too if he was not sure about them,
he brings only one asham.
If he found out in between,
just as he brings a chatas
for each and every one,
so too he brings an asham taluy
for each and every one.
Just as if he ate chelev, blood,
nosar, and piggul in one time of forgetting,
he must bring a chatas for each and every one,

chunks.he: כָּךְ עַל לֹא הוֹדַע שֶׁלָּהֶן מֵבִיא
chunks.en: so too if he was not sure about them, he brings

chunks.he: אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
chunks.en: an asham taluy for each and every one.
If chelev and nosar were in front of him,
and he ate one of them and does not
know which one he ate;
if his wife, who was niddah, and his sister were with him in the house,
and he sinned by mistake with one of them and does not
know with which one he sinned;

chunks.he: שַׁבָּת וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים וְעָשָׂה מְלָאכָה בֵּין
chunks.en: if Shabbos and Yom Kippur came one after the other, and he did work at

chunks.he: הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת וְאֵין יָדוּעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶם עָשָׂה.
chunks.en: twilight, and does not know on which day he did it:

words.note: The time between sunset and dark.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says he is free.
Rabbi Yosei said,
they did not argue about one who does
work at twilight,
that he is free,
because I say,
he did part of the work on one day,
and part of it on the next day.
So what did they argue about?
About one who did work in the middle of the day and does not
know whether he did it on Shabbos or
on Yom Kippur;
or about one who did work and does not know
which kind of melachah he did.
Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says he is free.
Rabbi Yehudah said,
Rabbi Yehoshua would free him
even from an asham taluy.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri and Rabbi Shimon explain what Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argued about. Rabbi Yehudah gives the example of one who meant to pick figs on Shabbos and picked grapes.

chunks.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שְׁזוּרִי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים,
chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri and Rabbi Shimon say,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Shimon Shezuri say:

chunks.en: they did not argue about a thing
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree with regard to a case involving a matter

chunks.en: that is all one kind of sin,
chunks.st: where his lack of knowledge involves items from one category,
chunks.stMore: e.g., he picked a grape from a vine on Shabbat and does not know which vine it was,

chunks.en: that he is liable.
chunks.st: as in that case they both agree that he is liable, since he knows the nature of his sin.

chunks.en: So what did they argue about?
chunks.st: With regard to what case did they disagree?

chunks.he: עַל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת,
chunks.en: About a thing that is two kinds of sins,
chunks.st: With regard to a case involving a matter where his lack of knowledge involves items from two categories,
chunks.stMore: e.g., he picked fruit from a tree on Shabbat and does not know whether it was from a vine or from a fig tree.

chunks.en: where Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas
chunks.st: As, in that case Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin offering, since he certainly sinned,

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua says he is free.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Yehoshua deems him exempt, as he does not know the nature of his sin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ נִתְכַּוֵּן לְלַקֵּט תְּאֵנִים וְלִקֵּט עֲנָבִים,
chunks.en: Even if he meant to pick figs on Shabbos and picked grapes,
chunks.st: Even if one intended to pick figs and he picked grapes,

chunks.en: or meant grapes and picked figs,
chunks.st: or to pick grapes and he picked figs,

chunks.en: or black figs and picked white ones,
chunks.st: or to pick black figs and he picked white figs,

chunks.en: or white ones and picked black ones,
chunks.st: or to pick white figs and he picked black figs,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says he must bring a chatas,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable to bring a sin offering

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehoshua says he is free.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Yehoshua deems him exempt.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda added:

chunks.en: "I wonder if Rabbi Yehoshua would free him
chunks.st: I wonder if

chunks.en: in this case."
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua deemed him exempt in that case, as even in his opinion the person intended to perform a prohibited labor.

chunks.en: If so,
chunks.st: The mishna asks: If it is so, that he is not exempt according to Rabbi Yehuda,

chunks.en: why does it say (Vayikra 4),
chunks.st: why is it stated:

chunks.en: "his sin which he sinned"?
chunks.st: “If his sin, wherein he has sinned” (Leviticus 4:23),
chunks.stMore: from which it is derived that one is liable only if the object of the sin was the one that he intended?

chunks.en: That comes to leave out one who was not paying attention at all.
chunks.st: The mishna answers: This serves to exclude one who acts unawares and does not intend to perform a prohibited action at all.

words.en: one who is busy (not paying attention)

mishnayos.summary: Which kinds of blood is it forbidden to eat, with the punishment of kares? This mishnah lists the blood one is liable for and the blood one is not.

chunks.en: Blood from shechting a farm animal,
chunks.st: If one consumed an olive-bulk of blood that spurted during the slaughter of a domesticated animal,

chunks.en: a wild animal, or birds,
chunks.st: an undomesticated animal, or a bird,

chunks.en: whether non-kosher or kosher,
chunks.st: whether it is a kosher or non-kosher species;

chunks.en: blood from stabbing,
chunks.st: or if one consumed blood that flowed after stabbing an animal or killing it in a manner other than by ritual slaughter,

mishnayos.summary: A sure asham, an ox that is to be stoned, and an eglah arufah are different from an asham taluy. This mishnah explains what happens to each one when it turns out it was not needed.

chunks.en: A sure asham is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of a definite guilt offering, it is not so,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the halakha is different than with regard to a provisional guilt offering.

chunks.en: If it was before it was shechted,
chunks.st: If he made the discovery that he did not sin before the ram was slaughtered,

chunks.stMore: as it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: Once it was shechted, it must be buried.
chunks.st: If it became known to him that he did not sin after the ram was slaughtered, it shall be buried
chunks.stMore: like a non-sacred animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, and its blood is poured.

chunks.en: If the blood was sprinkled,
chunks.st: If he discovered that he did not sin after the blood was sprinkled,

chunks.en: the meat goes out to be burned.
chunks.st: the flesh shall go out to the place of burning,
chunks.stMore: like any disqualified offering.

chunks.en: An ox that is to be stoned is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of an ox that is sentenced to be stoned (see Exodus 21:28–32), e.g., for killing a person, it is not so,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it also does not have the same halakhic status as a provisional guilt offering.

chunks.stMore: as it never had the status of an ox sentenced to be stoned.

chunks.en: Once it was stoned, one may benefit from it.
chunks.st: If this was discovered after the ox was stoned, its halakhic status is as though it had not been sentenced, and therefore deriving benefit from its carcass is permitted.

chunks.en: An eglah arufah is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of a heifer whose neck is broken, when a corpse is found between two cities and the identity of the murderer is unknown (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9), it is not so
chunks.stMore: i.e., the halakha is different than with regard to a provisional guilt offering.

words.note: The eglah arufah is brought when a killed person is found and no one knows who did it.

chunks.en: If it was found out before its neck was broken,
chunks.st: If the identity of the murderer is discovered before the heifer’s neck was broken,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock,
chunks.stMore: as it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: Once its neck was broken, it is buried in its place,
chunks.st: But if the identity of the murderer was discovered after the heifer’s neck was broken, it shall be buried in its place,
chunks.stMore: like any other heifer whose neck is broken.

chunks.en: because from the start it came for a doubt,
chunks.st: The reason is that from the outset the heifer whose neck is broken comes to atone for a situation of uncertainty.

chunks.en: it atoned for its doubt, and that is done.
